source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which exercise helps a client in a leg cast maintain thigh muscle strength?
questions.rationale: Isometric quadriceps and gluteal setting prevent atrophy without moving the part.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Exercise and Disuse (PDF p. 444)
questions.quote: Quadriceps contraction exercises (tightening the muscles of the thigh)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which client is not a candidate for MRI?
questions.rationale: Metal implants, clips, or pacemakers contraindicate MRI.
questions.quote: Patient with any metal implants, clips, or pacemakers are not candidates for MRI.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Before a bone scan, the client should:
questions.rationale: A full bladder interferes with pelvic imaging; drink fluids to distribute isotope.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bone Scan (PDF p. 444)
questions.quote: The patient is asked to empty the bladder before the procedure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After knee arthroscopy, the nurse should:
questions.rationale: Compression dressing, ice, extension and elevation; monitor neurovascular status.
questions.quote: Frequently, the joint is kept extended and elevated to reduce swelling.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Normal synovial fluid obtained by arthrocentesis is:
questions.rationale: Normal synovial fluid is clear, pale, straw colored, and scanty.
questions.quote: Normally, synovial fluid is clear, pale, straw colored, and scanty in volume.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a wet plaster cast be handled?
questions.rationale: Use palms to avoid dents; leave uncovered on soft surface to dry.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cast Care (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Handle damp plaster cast with palms of the hands

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How long does a plaster cast take to dry completely?
questions.rationale: Plaster: 24–72 hours; fiberglass dries in 10–15 minutes.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Casting Materials (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Requires 24 to 72 hours to dry completely

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a new cast reports warmth during application. The nurse explains:
questions.rationale: Prepare the client for warmth as the cast sets.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cast Care (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: prepare the patient for the sensation of increasing warmth

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with a cast complains of itching underneath. The nurse advises:
questions.rationale: Use cool air from a hair dryer; never insert objects.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cast Care (PDF p. 448)
questions.quote: Blow cool air from hair dryer

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client in a cast has pain unrelieved by elevation and analgesics. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Unrelieved pain may indicate compartment syndrome; report immediately.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cast Care (PDF p. 448)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: For suspected compartment syndrome under a cast, the extremity should be:
questions.rationale: Elevate no higher than heart level; bivalve the cast; fasciotomy may be needed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Compartment Syndrome (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: Extremity must be elevated no higher than heart level

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Cutting a cast lengthwise into two halves to relieve tightness is:
questions.rationale: Bivalving relieves tightness; windowing allows wound inspection.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Cast Techniques (PDF p. 447)
questions.quote: Cutting the cast into two halves

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A warm spot on the cast with foul odor suggests:
questions.rationale: Warmth, drainage, and odor indicate skin breakdown; window the cast.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: A warm area on the cast or brace suggests underlying tissue erythema

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Contracture of fingers and wrist from obstructed forearm arterial flow is:
questions.rationale: Volkmann's ischemic contracture is a type of compartment syndrome.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Immobilized Extremities (PDF p. 450)
questions.quote: Volkmann's contracture, a specific type of compartment syndrome

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which brace is used for scoliosis?

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A Dennis Browne splint is used for:
questions.rationale: Dennis Browne shoe corrects talipes equinovarus.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A cock-up splint is applied for:
questions.rationale: Cock-up splint supports the wrist in radial nerve palsy.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding in a casted limb is normal?
questions.rationale: Normal: minimal edema, pink, warm, rapid capillary refill, normal sensation.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Neurovascular Checks (PDF p. 449)
questions.quote: pink color, warm to touch, rapid capillary refill response
